scenes.headline: How sliding-window attention keeps a cache small
scenes.sub: Local layers, a global layer every few, and a sink
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Quenby! The cheapest way to stop attention growing is to stop it looking far back.

steps.label: global layer
steps.say: A normal layer lets each query see every earlier key. A growing triangle.

steps.label: local layer
steps.term: Window: the last W keys only
steps.say: A local layer keeps only a band, the last few keys. Every query reads the same amount.

steps.label: the sink column
steps.say: Many models also keep the first token visible to everyone. More on that soon.
One window layer sees a window back.
Stack another, and each position already summarises the window before it.
Mistral's paper puts it at about one hundred and thirty-one thousand tokens, with a window of four thousand and ninety-six. In theory.
Longformer drew the band in twenty twenty.

steps.caption: a window plus a few global tokens
steps.say: And added a few global positions. Today's models add whole global layers instead.

scenes.quote: fails when the text length surpasses the cache size
scenes.say: Window attention fails when the text length surpasses the cache size.

scenes.title: Why it fails, and the fix

items.say: A softmax has to put its weight somewhere, even when nothing matters.

items.text: Models dump it on token one
items.say: Trained models park it on the first tokens, which every query can see.
Slide them out of the window, and that weight lands anywhere.
So keep the first four tokens forever. StreamingLLM ran four million tokens that way.

steps.say: Modern models interleave. MiMo stacks five window layers of just a hundred and twenty-eight tokens under one global layer, eight times.
The global layers carry every long-range lookup. The windows carry everything local, at a fixed cost.

scenes.title: Gemma 4 31B cache at 262,144 tokens, GB
scenes.say: Gemma 4 does it one in six. Fifty window layers hold under a gigabyte. Made full, the same model would need two hundred and twenty-five.

scenes.text: A window caps memory by position; a global layer every few reads the whole past.
scenes.say: A window caps memory by position. A global layer every few reads the whole past.

recap: A band of W keys per query
Keep a sink, or it falls apart
Windows below, a global layer above
scenes.say: A band, a sink, and a global layer every few. Thanks for watching!
